title: Property (S_k) ascends along flat maps with (S_k) fibres
statement: Let $\varphi:R\to S$ be a homomorphism of commutative rings and $k\ge0$ an integer. Assume (1) $R$ is Noetherian [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring], (2) $S$ is Noetherian, (3) $\varphi$ is flat [def-weil-pbc-flat-ring-map], (4) for every prime $\mathfrak p\subset R$ the fibre ring $S\otimes_R\kappa(\mathfrak p)$ [def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime] (a Noetherian ring) has property $(S_k)$ [def-weil-pbc-serre-conditions-rk-sk], and (5) $R$ has property $(S_k)$. Then $S$ has property $(S_k)$.

source.place: Algebra, Lemma Tag 0339 (lemma-Sk-goes-up, line 46403) and its proof (via Lemma Tag 0337 lemma-apply-grothendieck, depth formula for flat local maps, and Lemma Tag 00OM lemma-dimension-base-fibre-total)

proof.text: *Setting.* Let $\mathfrak q\subset S$ be a prime ideal and $\mathfrak p=\varphi^{-1}(\mathfrak q)$, a prime of $R$. By [def-weil-pbc-serre-conditions-rk-sk] ($S$ is Noetherian by (2)) we must show $\operatorname{depth}(S_{\mathfrak q})\ge\min\{k,\dim(S_{\mathfrak q})\}$. By [lem-weil-pbc-flat-local-ring-maps] ($\varphi$ flat by (3), $R$, $S$ Noetherian by (1), (2)), the induced map $\varphi_{\mathfrak q}:R_{\mathfrak p}\to S_{\mathfrak q}$, $r/s\mapsto\varphi(r)/\varphi(s)$, is a flat local homomorphism of Noetherian local rings.

*Closed fibre of $\varphi_{\mathfrak q}$.* The maximal ideal of $R_{\mathfrak p}$ is $\mathfrak pR_{\mathfrak p}$ [def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime]; the ideal of $S_{\mathfrak q}$ it generates under $\varphi_{\mathfrak q}$ is generated by the elements $\varphi(a)/\varphi(s)=(\varphi(a)/1)\varphi(s)^{-1}$ ($a\in\mathfrak p$, $s\in R\setminus\mathfrak p$; $\varphi(s)\notin\mathfrak q$ is a unit of $S_{\mathfrak q}$), so it is the ideal $\mathfrak pS_{\mathfrak q}$ generated by the $\varphi(a)/1$, $a\in\mathfrak p$. Hence the closed fibre of $\varphi_{\mathfrak q}$ is $S_{\mathfrak q}/\mathfrak pS_{\mathfrak q}$.

source.place: Algebra, Lemma 0339, proof (the closed fibre written as S_q/pS_q)

proof.text: *Depth formula.* By [lem-weil-pbc-flat-local-depth-formula] applied to the flat local homomorphism $\varphi_{\mathfrak q}:R_{\mathfrak p}\to S_{\mathfrak q}$ of Noetherian local rings (step 1), whose closed fibre is $S_{\mathfrak q}/\mathfrak pS_{\mathfrak q}$ (step 2): $\operatorname{depth}(S_{\mathfrak q})=\operatorname{depth}(R_{\mathfrak p})+\operatorname{depth}(S_{\mathfrak q}/\mathfrak pS_{\mathfrak q})$.

source.place: Algebra, Lemma 0339, proof, first display (by Lemma 0337, lemma-apply-grothendieck)

proof.text: *Dimension.* By [lem-weil-pbc-flat-height-formula] ($\varphi$ flat, $R$ and $S$ Noetherian, $\mathfrak p=\varphi^{-1}(\mathfrak q)$): $\dim(S_{\mathfrak q})=\dim(R_{\mathfrak p})+\dim(S_{\mathfrak q}/\mathfrak pS_{\mathfrak q})$. Only the inequality $\dim(S_{\mathfrak q})\le\dim(R_{\mathfrak p})+\dim(S_{\mathfrak q}/\mathfrak pS_{\mathfrak q})$ is used below; this is the inequality the source takes from Lemma 00OM, and it notes that equality holds by Lemma 00ON, which is the cited node (a Mathlib leaf).

source.place: Algebra, Lemma 0339, proof, second display (Lemma 00OM, lemma-dimension-base-fibre-total; equality by 00ON, lemma-dimension-base-fibre-equals-total, as the proof remarks)

proof.text: *The fibre term.* Let $C=S\otimes_R\kappa(\mathfrak p)$ be the fibre ring [def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime] and $j:S\to C$, $s\mapsto s\otimes1$. $C$ is Noetherian by [lem-weil-pbc-fibre-ring-noetherian] ($S$ Noetherian), and has property $(S_k)$ by hypothesis (4). Since $\varphi^{-1}(\mathfrak q)=\mathfrak p$, [lem-weil-pbc-fibre-ring-primes-bijection] gives a prime $\mathfrak Q\subset C$ with $j^{-1}(\mathfrak Q)=\mathfrak q$, and [lem-weil-pbc-fibre-ring-local-ring-iso] (with $A=R$, $B=S$) gives a ring isomorphism $C_{\mathfrak Q}\cong S_{\mathfrak q}/\mathfrak pS_{\mathfrak q}$. By $(S_k)$ for $C$ [def-weil-pbc-serre-conditions-rk-sk], $\operatorname{depth}(C_{\mathfrak Q})\ge\min\{k,\dim(C_{\mathfrak Q})\}$. A ring isomorphism carries maximal ideals, regular sequences [def-weil-pbc-depth] and chains of primes to each other, so depth and Krull dimension agree on both sides: $\operatorname{depth}(S_{\mathfrak q}/\mathfrak pS_{\mathfrak q})\ge\min\{k,\dim(S_{\mathfrak q}/\mathfrak pS_{\mathfrak q})\}$.

source.place: Algebra, Lemma 0339, proof ('as the fibre rings of the map are assumed (S_k)'); the identification S_q/pS_q = (S tensor kappa(p))_q is Algebra, Definition before Lemma 00OM (line 27380)

proof.text: *The base term.* $R$ is Noetherian and has $(S_k)$ (hypotheses (1), (5)), so by [def-weil-pbc-serre-conditions-rk-sk] at the prime $\mathfrak p$: $\operatorname{depth}(R_{\mathfrak p})\ge\min\{k,\dim(R_{\mathfrak p})\}$.

source.place: Algebra, Lemma 0339, proof (hypothesis (5) in the chain of inequalities)

proof.text: *Conclusion.* Write $a=\dim(R_{\mathfrak p})$, $b=\dim(S_{\mathfrak q}/\mathfrak pS_{\mathfrak q})$ in $\{0,1,\dots\}\cup\{\infty\}$. By steps 3, 5, 6, $\operatorname{depth}(S_{\mathfrak q})\ge\min\{k,b\}+\min\{k,a\}$. This is $\ge\min\{k,a+b\}$: if $a\ge k$ or $b\ge k$ the left side is $\ge k$; otherwise $a,b<k$ are finite and the left side is $a+b$. By step 4, $a+b\ge\dim(S_{\mathfrak q})$, so $\min\{k,a+b\}\ge\min\{k,\dim(S_{\mathfrak q})\}$. Hence $\operatorname{depth}(S_{\mathfrak q})\ge\min\{k,\dim(S_{\mathfrak q})\}$; as $\mathfrak q$ was arbitrary, $S$ has property $(S_k)$ [def-weil-pbc-serre-conditions-rk-sk].
